item.title: Texans star celebrates Abbott's defeat with an NSFW message
item.description: Dalton Schultz, who has been with the Houston Texans since 2023 has let his feelings towards Greg Abbott known. (Tim Warner/Getty Images) This Texans star has a blunt message for Greg Abbott after the longtime Texas governor's election defeat. Texas was swept up in a blue wave on Tuesday night, with Democrats breaking the hold Republicans had on Texas politics for the past 30 years. Texans tight end Dalton Schultz celebrated the news by giving the outgoing Texas governor a two-word send-off on his Instagram story. "Get F---ed!," Schultz wrote on his Instagram story on Wednesday morning, tagging Abbott in the post. The Texans player followed up his insult to Abbott by showing his support for the newly elected Texas governor, Gina Hinojosa. Reactions to Schultz's position surprised fans who were unaware of Schultz political standing, with many fans saying his post warranted a jersey purchase "That's my tight end," one fan wrote on X. "Damn, no more Dalton Schultzslander lol," another fan wrote. "We have our Joe Rogan of the Left," another chimed in. AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 3: Gov. Greg Abbott hugs his wife, Cecilia, and their daughter, Audrey, after delivering a concession speech during an election night event at Speakeasy in Austin on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (Jay Janner/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images) (Austin American-Statesman/Hearst/Austin American-Statesman via Ge) Schultz, who has been with the Texans since 2023 after spending four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys, holds the franchise record for most receptions by a tight end. He has also made his opinions about Greg Abbott and his policies abundantly clear for some time now. In a tweet from February 23, 2022, Schultz criticized Abbott for issuing a directive ordering the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services to treat and classify medically necessary gender affirming care for transgender youth as child abuse "If you think anything about what the POS [Greg Abbott] is doing about Trans kids in Texas is ok or justified, please unfollow me," Schultz wrote on X. If you think anything about what the POS @GregAbbott_TX is doing about Trans kids in Texas is ok or justified, please unfollow me. - Dalton Schultz (@BinghamBaller9) February 23, 2022 In July 2022, Schultz called out the Texas governor once again, quoting a tweet from the official Texas governor account blaming the deaths of migrants on President Joe Biden. Never heard of a good leader who points fingers, Greg. - Dalton Schultz (@BinghamBaller9) June 28, 2022 Schultz, who graduated from Stanford University in 2017, also criticized the two-party system that exists in the United States in May of 2022, calling it "broken" and "beyond frustrating as a US citizen." His political posting on X has slowed since 2022, but the Texas Democrats' massive victory and Greg Abbott's defeat apparently warranted a social media victory lap. item.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
item.description: Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms. The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students. Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on. Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date. The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine. If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.” “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote. More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices. In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages. Students were shown starter prompts tied to their specific class and assignment, offering guided help or study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards built from their course materials. The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini. New York and Los Angeles both announced plans in September to restrict access to AI tools on school devices. “We are reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Unified School District told AFP. The spokesperson said the district believes AI can improve teaching and learning if it is introduced carefully and with clear safeguards, and pointed to district principles requiring that technology support rather than replace teachers and protect student privacy. In a statement on X, Google said Tuesday’s changes give “schools more choice, not less.” “We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google said. The post Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kyle Farmer’s 2026 Season: A Short Stint With Big Wasted Potential
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Farmer spent most of 2026 on the Atlanta Braves roster, yet he barely touched the field. The veteran infielder arrived in early February hoping to help his hometown club, but his time in the big leagues was short and quiet. He played only 14 games all season, a number that shocked fans who expected him to be a key backup. His path from signing to release tells a story of missed chances and a roster that simply did not need him. The Braves brought him in as a free agent in early February 2026, only to cut him and re-sign him a month later in March. Per Battery Power , he was meant to be an end-of-bench option who could fill in at shortstop or catch in an emergency. Instead, he sat on the bench for weeks, saw limited action, and landed on the injured list by mid-May. When he returned on July 4, he got just one plate appearance before the team released him on July 21. He signed a minor league deal later and came back in September, but his season was already over. A Roster Spot That Went Unused Farmer made the Opening Day roster, but that spot meant little when he could not get into games. He played ten games over six weeks and got only 15 plate appearances. His return in July lasted two games with one at-bat before he was let go. Even his late-season call-up in September brought just two games and three more plate appearances. In total, he slashed .222/.211/.278 with a 25 wRC+, numbers that show he could not hit at all. He finished with -0.1 fWAR, marking his second straight season below replacement level. On April 30, acting as the designated hitter at home versus the Detroit Tigers, he made his single start. He went 1-for-3 in that game, which was his best moment of the year. That single in the second inning helped score the first run, giving him a win probability added of 0.03. Per Battery Power, it has been two years since Farmer actually provided any value to a team. It was a tiny spark in a very dark season for a player who has played 97 or more games every year since 2019, except for 2020. Why The Experiment Failed The Braves hoped Farmer would be a safety net if Ha-Seong Kim got hurt, but the plan fell apart. He spent 2025 with the Colorado Rockies and had a terrible year with a -1.0 fWAR in 300 plate appearances. That bad season hurt his reputation before he even put on a Braves uniform. The team needed someone who could hit or play great defense, and Farmer did neither in his tiny sample. He played third base, second base, and shortstop but did nothing to stand out in any of those spots. At 36 years old, Farmer is past his prime, and the stats prove it. His career has been built on playing a lot of games, but he could not do that in 2026. The team gave him a chance to return to Atlanta, but they did not give him a real role to fill. He was supposed to be a utility guy, but he ended up being a bench warmer who got released in July. The numbers show he was not ready to help the team when they needed him

Now, he has two straight bad years and a 2026 season where he played only 14 games. The Braves will need to find a new utility player who can actually hit or play defense if they want to improve their bench depth. As the team looks ahead to 2027, they must focus on finding players who can contribute right away.

item.title: Malachi Toney injury update: Latest news on Miami star's status for Notre Dame clash
item.description: Malachi Toney injury update: Latest news on Miami star's status for Notre Dame clash originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Notre Dame is favored at home in a massive matchup with Miami, but the Hurricanes have the advantage when it comes to star power — at least, as long as Malachi Toney can play. Toney is dealing with an injury ahead of Saturday's clash with the Fighting Irish, threatening both Miami's chances of going into South Bend as healthy as possible offensively and the sophomore receiver's chance to make his case to Heisman Trophy voters. Toney has seven touchdowns in his last three games and has already hit the 1,000-yard mark through just eight games. Here's what you need to know about Toney's injury and his status for Saturday. MORE: Previewing biggest matchups on loaded Week 10 slate Malachi Toney injury update Toney's status for Saturday's game is "uncertain" due to an ankle injury, ESPN's Pete Thamel reports. Despite the concerning news, Thamel says Toney is "expected to press and attempt to play." NEWS: Miami star Malachi Toney is dealing with an injured ankle and his status for Saturday’s game against Notre Dame is uncertain, sources tell me and @max_olson. Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game. https://t.co/Uo38qFaLM8 — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) November 4, 2026 Thamel later included a statement from Miami in his reporting on the injury, which confirmed Toney "sustained an injury" and that he is undergoing medical evaluation. The school added that it would "share additional information as appropriate." Update from Miami: “Malachi Toney sustained an injury during Wednesday’s practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team’s medical staff. We will share additional updates as appropriate.” https://t.co/HOVpG8AF1H — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) November 4, 2026 The injury occurred during practice on Wednesday, according to On3's Pete Nakos , who echoes Thamel's reporting that Toney is already "pushing to play" against Notre Dame. The Miami Herald's Barry Jackson reported Toney's injury is "not serious," adding that one Miami coach is hopeful the star receiver will be back on the practice field Thursday. I was giving UM more time to respond to my tip earlier, but they decided not to, which I understand. Someone at UM practice said earlier today that Toney was "banged up" with the ankle injury but it's not serious. A UM coach has told friends that he's hopeful Malachi will be back tomorrow and play Saturday. Injury is not serious/longterm. — Barry Jackson (@flasportsbuzz) November 4, 2026 Toney is the heart of Miami's offense outside of QB Darian Mensah, as he is averaging 128.4 yards per game and has 13 touchdowns in just eight games after a stellar true freshman season. If Toney is forced to sit out, his momentum in what many view as a three-man Heisman race with Mensah and Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith would

item.title: Caitlin Clark reacts to encouraging Jack Campbell news
item.description: Oct 1, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) walks on the court during the fourth quarter of game three of the first round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs against the Las Vegas Aces at Michelob Ultra Arena. Mandatory Credit: Lucas Peltier-Imagn Images Many football fans have been keeping an eye on the story of Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, who suffered a frightening neck injury during Sunday’s game. Caitlin Clark has added incentive to monitor Campbell’s progress. Not only are she and the 2025 All-Pro both Iowa Hawkeyes, but Campbell’s wife Megan played with Clark at Iowa during the 2020-21 season. On Wednesday afternoon, after Campbell announced he had full movement in his lower extremities and was “continuing to make progress” with moving his upper body, Clark sent a quick message of support to her former teammate. On her Instagram story , Clark shared ESPN and Adam Schefter’s post featuring Jack Campbell’s statement. Underneath it, she commented three blue hearts and tagged Megan. Once a Hawkeye Megan Campbell (née Meyer) was a star high school player in Mason City, Iowa before joining the Iowa program in 2019. In 2020-21, she was a key contributor off the bench while Clark became the team’s freshman sensation, scoring 26.6 points per game and leading the Hawkeyes to the Sweet 16. While Meyer transferred to Drake following the season and enjoyed a stellar 2021-22 campaign, she and Clark obviously still have a connection, judging by the latter’s social media post. ‘Optimistic’ Campbell working toward recovery Jack Campbell went down while making a tackle in the fourth quarter of the Lions’ win over the Minnesota Vikings. The 26-year-old linebacker lay motionless on the field for several minutes before being immobilized and taken off on a stretcher. The Lions had been vague on specifics regarding Campbell’s condition, only saying Monday that things were trending positively. Campbell himself provided the details in a statement earlier today. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better,” he said. “My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.” The post Caitlin Clark reacts to encouraging Jack Campbell news appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Purple wave, blue wave: Valkyries parade doubles as election celebration
item.description: Valkyries' mascot Violet waves to fans in attendance to see the 2026 WNBA Champions at Jack London Square in Oakland, Calif. on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Following the ceremony, the team will bring the WNBA Championship Trophy across the Bay to San Francisco for the parade. (Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle) Giddy energy from Tuesday night's Democratic electoral sweep seemed only to grow Wednesday morning as revelers gathered for the Valkyries WNBA championship parade. That much was clear from the sign that Serena Poon held aloft as she stood on the ferry lawn at Jack London Square, where the players and their entourage would soon depart by boat to San Francisco. "Purple wave 10/31; Blue wave 11/2," it said, linking the team's come-from-behind victory on Halloween night to a national blowout by Democrats, one so overwhelming that pundits ran out of tidal metaphors to describe it. The connection seemed fitting when a procession of Democratic politicians strode down the Embarcadero to welcome the Valkyries players when their boat was set to dock near the Ferry Building at noon. Among the delegation: Sen. Adam Schiff, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, state Sen. Scott Wiener (who is now leading in the race to succeed Pelosi) and Mayor Daniel Lurie in a violet shirt. For Poon, the political contact high was palpable. "We're just riding the high of Valks win, and then last night was just historic with blue wave," she said. "It was like a blue tsunami, and I'm just so stoked." Every Embarcadero-bound BART train and Muni bus became a purple and black menagerie as fans flocked in with jerseys, feathery boas and birdlike headdresses. If the attire seemed apolitical, the placards were not. Beth Jaeger of San Francisco arrived at the Embarcadero at 8 a.m. dressed as a Valkyrie, complete with purple face paint - and a sign that said "In a world of Sophies, be a Gabby." The slogan referenced public comments by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has insisted that trans women should be barred from the WNBA. Henry, from Oakland, holds a sign celebrating both the Valkyries' championship and Democrats' sweeping wins in Tuesday's midterm election. (Saul Pink / S.F. Chronicle) On the back of Jaeger's sign: "Welcome to the Gay Area." Others echoed pro-LGBTQ messages that, while not directly tied to an election wedge issue on Tuesday, generally defied the Trump Administration's stances on gender politics and diversity. As the morning wore on, "Gay Area" logos proliferated along the Embarcadero: in shimmery ink on card stock, emblazoned on T-shirts, embroidered on denim jackets, scrawled onto decals. "It was already so hopeful to see them win, and then to see and then to see so much hope across the country," said Cat De La Pena of San Jose, dangling her own hand-made "Gay Area" sign with a portrait of Valkyries forward and championship MVP Gabby Williams, arms outstretched to sink a 3-pointer into the basket. Williams isn't the only player to become a mascot
item.content:encoded: Valkyries' mascot Violet waves to fans in attendance to see the 2026 WNBA Champions at Jack London Square in Oakland, Calif. on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Following the ceremony, the team will bring the WNBA Championship Trophy across the Bay to San Francisco for the parade. (Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle) Giddy energy from Tuesday night's Democratic electoral sweep seemed only to grow Wednesday morning as revelers gathered for the Valkyries WNBA championship parade. That much was clear from the sign that Serena Poon held aloft as she stood on the ferry lawn at Jack London Square, where the players and their entourage would soon depart by boat to San Francisco. "Purple wave 10/31; Blue wave 11/2," it said, linking the team's come-from-behind victory on Halloween night to a national blowout by Democrats, one so overwhelming that pundits ran out of tidal metaphors to describe it. The connection seemed fitting when a procession of Democratic politicians strode down the Embarcadero to welcome the Valkyries players when their boat was set to dock near the Ferry Building at noon. Among the delegation: Sen. Adam Schiff, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, state Sen. Scott Wiener (who is now leading in the race to succeed Pelosi) and Mayor Daniel Lurie in a violet shirt. For Poon, the political contact high was palpable. "We're just riding the high of Valks win, and then last night was just historic with blue wave," she said. "It was like a blue tsunami, and I'm just so stoked." Every Embarcadero-bound BART train and Muni bus became a purple and black menagerie as fans flocked in with jerseys, feathery boas and birdlike headdresses. If the attire seemed apolitical, the placards were not. Beth Jaeger of San Francisco arrived at the Embarcadero at 8 a.m. dressed as a Valkyrie, complete with purple face paint - and a sign that said "In a world of Sophies, be a Gabby." The slogan referenced public comments by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has insisted that trans women should be barred from the WNBA. Henry, from Oakland, holds a sign celebrating both the Valkyries' championship and Democrats' sweeping wins in Tuesday's midterm election. (Saul Pink / S.F. Chronicle) On the back of Jaeger's sign: "Welcome to the Gay Area." Others echoed pro-LGBTQ messages that, while not directly tied to an election wedge issue on Tuesday, generally defied the Trump Administration's stances on gender politics and diversity. As the morning wore on, "Gay Area" logos proliferated along the Embarcadero: in shimmery ink on card stock, emblazoned on T-shirts, embroidered on denim jackets, scrawled onto decals. "It was already so hopeful to see them win, and then to see and then to see so much hope across the country," said Cat De La Pena of San Jose, dangling her own hand-made "Gay Area" sign with a portrait of Valkyries forward and championship MVP Gabby Williams, arms outstretched to sink a 3-pointer into the basket. Williams isn't the only player to become a mascot and de facto ambassador for progressive ideals. "I think Kiah Stokes swept Iowa herself," De La Pena's friend remarked, referring to the team's center, who hails from the battleground state, where Democrat Rob Sand flipped the governor's seat Tuesday night. Bee Garcia, 27, stood in front of the barricade near the beginning of the parade holding a sign that praised the team and its support for the queer community, while also celebrating transit systems that won big after Bay Area voters approved a pair of tax measures to shore up their operating budgets. "My MUNI is quick, My AC is trans, My team 4 the Gays, Our Valks are Champs!" Garcia's sign said. Flanked by friends who got her "obsessed" with the team this season, Garcia explained why her attachment feels overtly political. Bee Garcia, 27, of San Francisco, holds a sign at the Valkyries parade. (Matthias Gafni / S.F. Chronicle) "They're very open about who they are and they are open about being queer and supporting the trans community," she said. Shalom Kimble of San Francisco wove many political statements into her purple-and-gray coveralls, which featured buttons supporting Black Lives Matter and decrying ICE, a rainbow heart pride patch, and a sparkling "For the Gays" inscription on the back. Kimble carried a to-go coffee cup from a Ferry Building cafe where every customer in line had been talking politics, she said. "It just all came together," she said, referring to the convergence of sunny weather and Democratic winds on the day of the parade. Brad Porter and Colleen Johnston, a couple from Walnut Creek, reverted to more traditional symbolism to show their Democratic pride on the Embarcadero. Although both wore Valkyries-themed apparel, they waved old-school American flags. The pair hadn't initially planned to bring politics to the festivities on Wednesday, Porter said. "We just felt so exuberant after the results came in" Tuesday night. Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Giants injury update: Cam Skattebo, Abdul Carter still not practicing
item.description: Cam Skattebo | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo remains day to day with a hamstring injury, and edge defender Abdul Carter is still sidelined by an illness. Neither player participated in practice Wednesday as the Giants prepared for Sunday’s gane against the Philadelphia Eagles. Skattebo intentionally went to the ground when he felt a twinge in his hamstring at the end of a 42-yard run late in the Giants’ Week 7 victory over the Houston Texans. Tyrone Tracy also suffered a hamstring injury in that game that was severe enough to land him on injured reserve for at least four weeks. Head coach John Harbaugh said “we’ll see” when asked on Wednesday if Skattebo would be able to play vs. Philadelphia. Skattebo did work with a trainer during practice. If Skattebo cannot play, Devin Singletary would start with newly-acquired Gregory Desrosiers, making his NFL debut, as the primary backup. The Giants also have running backs Phil Mafah and Eric Gray on the practice squad. As for Carter, Harbaugh said he “should be fine” by Sunday. item.title: UPDATED: Chicago Bears 16-Man Practice Squad
item.description: Aug 1, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans defensive end Earnest Brown IV (99) goes through drills during training camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears have a 16-man practice squad, but the list will be fluid, and we’ll update it throughout the year. UPDATE (11/4): The Bears signed TE Stephen Carlson to the active roster and signed DE Earnest Brown IV to the practice squad. Caden Barnett, OG Christian Jones, OT Salvon Ahmed, RB Kaden Davis, WR J.P. Richardson, WR Scotty Miller, WR Qadir Ismail, TE Miller Moss, QB Wayne Matthews III, LB Buddy Johnson, LB Keidron Smith, S Elijah Jones, CB KC Eziomume, CB Josh Butler, CB Earnest Brown IV, DE Beau Gardner, LS Practice squad injured: Anthony Johnson Jr. (S) Here are the qualifications for practice squad eligibility and some rules to remember. A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season. A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After the game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad. A player can be elevated up to three times, but if he’s needed after that, the team would be required to sign him to the 53-man active roster. Players on practice squads are free agents who can be signed to another team’s active roster. A player’s current club can’t block him from leaving; they can only make a counteroffer to keep him. Ultimately, it’s the player’s decision. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for three weeks, but if he’s released, he’ll revert to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks’ salary. A practice squad player can’t sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week.

item.title: Dianna Russini reportedly returning to sports media ‘next week’
item.description: Credit: The Dan Patrick Show Dianna Russini has apparently kept herself on the sidelines long enough. The former top NFL insider for The Athletic who became embroiled in scandal this offseason after numerous photos surfaced showing her cozy and seemingly intimate relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is set to return “next week” according to a report by Mike Florio in Pro Football Talk . “Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she’ll be returning to work ‘next week,'” Florio reports, indicating that it is “unclear” for what outlet she’ll be working for, or what job she will be doing. Russini resigned from The Athletic in April, one week after the New York Post published the first batch of photos showing her and Vrabel together at a high-end resort in Arizona. In her letter of resignation, Russini maintained that there was no foul play between her and Vrabel. “Rather than allowing this [scandal] to continue, I have decided to step aside now – before my current contract expires on June 30. I do so not because I accept the narrative that has been constructed around this episode, but because I refuse to lend it further oxygen or to let it define me or my career,” Russini wrote at the time. Last month, the New York Post reported that Russini had hired crisis management expert Melissa Nathan , one of the first signs that the veteran NFL reporter was eyeing a return to media. Russini has not made any public statements since her resignation in April. Whether Russini will return in a capacity that relies on her credibility as a reporter, or in a role that is more personality-focused, is unclear. No doubt, Russini maintains a large rolodex of contacts throughout the league, though those sources’ willingness to speak candidly with her might be compromised after the scandal. Russini has long been able to hold court in more casual settings, however, and would likely command an audience even without dishing out NFL scoops. The post Dianna Russini reportedly returning to sports media ‘next week’ appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Joe Scarborough goes after ESPN’s Pat McAfee: ‘It is a shame for the viewer’
item.description: Pat McAfee is a problem for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” Joe Scarborough of “Morning Joe” hammered away at Tuesday during election day. McAfee’s recent headline-grabbing issues with the University of Utah was the tipping point. “I’ve just had enough of this Pat McAfee ruining ‘College GameDay,’” Scarborough said Tuesday. “I look forward to waking up on Saturday mornings and watching that. ... It’s like he’s melting down. ... “It’s really ESPN. I mean, they run their company the way they want to run their company, but man, it is a shame for the viewer.” It's election day in America, and Morning Joe spent over two minutes discussing the country's most pressing issue: Pat McAfee ruining College GameDay "I don't know if they haven't gotten the message yet, but the manosphere that we all thought was brought in in '24, it may get… pic.twitter.com/a16be985Zt — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 3, 2026 McAfee revealed there have been death threats against him as a result of the controversy surrounding ESPN’s “College GameDay” visit to Utah. “I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DMs this month since these back to back days but ... I’m sure if I went in there now, I’d find some wishes for and threats of death for me,” McAfee posted on X. “‘Don’t read them.’ They’re everywhere.” The post includes screenshots from direct messages threatening violence against him and tweets expressing a desire to see him dead. The issue, according to Scarborough, is the show has gotten away from college football being played on Saturday and it’s more about itself. “I love watching Rece (Davis),” he said. “I love watching those guys and watching Nick (Saban) on there talking. ... Kirk Herbstreit’s amazing. Desmond (Howard) — they’re all great. And they’re all being eclipsed by ESPN’s just insatiable desire to give this guy more time.” “Maybe you aren’t having to be yelling at people and being freaked out because two kids in Utah put up signs or say something that might offend you,” Scarborough said. Meanwhile, McAfee said he felt “uncomfortable” after the University of Utah posted a since-deleted video of students “dogging” him. He also said the video shared by the university account was inciteful against him. McAfee cited the visit to the University of Utah reminded him of assassination of Charlie Kirk . Utah, for its part, apologized Monday. item.title: Valkyries star Gabby Williams reveals Michael Jordan reached out to her after WNBA championship win
item.description: Valkyries star Gabby Williams reveals Michael Jordan reached out to her after WNBA championship win originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michael Jordan knows a thing or two about winning, and Gabby Williams was in for a surprise of a lifetime when he reached out to congratulate her. The Golden State Valkyries star defeated the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, the first time that the league was pushed to the last qualifier round in the series. Williams, a forward for the Valkyries, shared that Jordan reached out to her to congratulate her on her first-ever WNBA championship win. “My Jordan rep agent texted me, and he was just like, ‘Just so you know, it’s not spam, but you’re gonna get a text,’ ” Williams told People about the moment. “And I was driving, and I was like, ‘Do not crash your car, do not crash your car. Get to the gym, get to the parking lot.’” Williams added that the six-time NBA champion praised her for becoming a WNBA champion. “He congratulated me, and said it’d been an amazing season and just told me, ‘Stay hungry.’ ” she told the outlet. “That felt like a very Michael Jordan thing to say.” Williams also left with the WNBA Finals MVP title after the thrilling 68–63 Game 7 victory over the Dream. She also praised their head coach, Natalie Nakase, for leading the team to the franchise's first-ever win. "Coach Nat is the most competitive person I've ever met in my entire life. But she is competitive in everything that she does, you know, even how she treats people, even how she shows up every day, and we all feed off of that," Williams said. "I think she's a leader by example. She cares so, so deeply on a human level for each person, and you just want to go through a wall for her." item.title: Meet the Shasta Family YMCA Athletes of the Week winners for Oct. 25-31
item.description: Two Shasta County athletes are being recognized for their outstanding achievements on the field and court. This week, Foothill and Redding Christian high school athletes are being highlighted. It's time to meet the two Shasta Family YMCA Athletes of the Week for their accomplishments over the week of Oct. 25-31. Turner Knowles, Foothill Sport : Football School : Foothill Class : Senior Team Contributions : Foothill running back Turner Knowles had a career day in a wild Week 9 win over Enterprise. Knowles rushed for 273 yards and 5 touchdowns — both set new career highs — to lead the Cougars to a 51-42 win over the Hornets. Knowles extended his season total to 1,277 yards and 21 touchdowns, good for the sixth most rushing yards and third most touchdowns scored by a skill position player. Knowles is one of the best running backs in the section, and he put it on display in the Cougars win over the Hornets. It was the second time Knowles rushed for over 200 yards this season and the third time he's scored at least 4 touchdowns in a game. Aliyah Mendoza, Redding Christian Sport : Volleyball School : Redding Christian Class : Senior Team Contributions : In the Lions Northern Section quarterfinal matchup against Fall River, senior outside hitter Aliyah Mendoza racked up 20 kills in four sets (5 kills per set) to help send her team to the semifinals. Mendoza also added 3 digs and 6 serve receptions in Redding Christian's 3-1 win over the Bulldogs. In a Nov. 3 win over Maxwell, Mendoza recorded 8 kills, 1 ace, 4 digs, 1 assist and 17 serve receptions as the Lions advanced to the Northern Section championship game. Mendoza's 257 kills this season rank 28th in the section and second in Division VI. Her 20 kills against Maxwell were the second most kills Mendoza has recorded in her varsity career. She helped lead the Lions to a 27-3 record and will compete for the NSCIF Division VI title on Saturday, Nov. 7. To nominate an athlete, please follow this link or submit nominations to sports reporter Brett Abrams at Brett.Abrams@redding.com . Brett Abrams is a sports reporter for the Record Searchlight/USA Today Network. He covers high school and local sports in the Redding area. Reach out to Brett with any sports tips or news on X (formerly Twitter) @brabrams_ or by email at Brett.Abrams@Redding.com . To support and sustain this work, please subscribe today. Thank you. Turner Knowles, Foothill Sport : Football School : Foothill Class : Senior Team Contributions : Foothill running back Turner Knowles had a career day in a wild Week 9 win over Enterprise. Knowles rushed for 273 yards and 5 touchdowns — both set new career highs — to lead the Cougars to a 51-42 win over the Hornets. Knowles extended his season total to 1,277 yards and 21 touchdowns, good for the sixth most rushing yards and third most touchdowns scored by a skill position player. Knowles is one of the best running backs in the section, and he put it on display in the Cougars win over the Hornets. It was the second time Knowles rushed for over 200 yards this season and the third time he's scored at least 4 touchdowns in a game. Aliyah Mendoza, Redding Christian Sport : Volleyball School : Redding Christian Class : Senior Team Contributions : In the Lions Northern Section quarterfinal matchup against Fall River, senior outside hitter Aliyah Mendoza racked up 20 kills in four sets (5 kills per set) to help send her team to the semifinals. Mendoza also added 3 digs and 6 serve receptions in Redding Christian's 3-1 win over the Bulldogs. In a Nov. 3 win over Maxwell, Mendoza recorded 8 kills, 1 ace, 4 digs, 1 assist and 17 serve receptions as the Lions advanced to the Northern Section championship game. Mendoza's 257 kills this season rank 28th in the section and second in Division VI. Her 20 kills against Maxwell were the second most kills Mendoza has recorded in her varsity career. She helped lead the Lions to a 27-3 record and will compete for the NSCIF Division VI title on Saturday, Nov. 7. item.title: 17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million
item.description: Dream bigger, babe. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty Images One of the basic problems of spending too much time on social media is that you are cooking your brain by reading posts from a pack of attention-seeking lunatics . If your social media of choice is the site formerly known as Twitter, and it is your main source of contact with the outside world , you may delusionally throw away nearly $500 million dollars on midterm elections, just like Elon Musk. In particular, $47 million of that money from Musk's America PAC was aimed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico, who trounced Musk's preferred Senate candidate, Ken Paxton, with 55 percent of the vote. Talarico even made Musk's influence a cent … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Brewers Should Avoid Signing Jake Bauers To Multi-Year Deal
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers Jake Bauers had a breakout season at 30 years old, and the Milwaukee Brewers extended him the qualifying offer. If Bauers accepts his one-year, $23.15 million offer, the Brewers don't have any choice to make. He will be back at that price. However, after the year he had, he should have a couple of multi-year offers on the table as well. The Brewers do not need to be one of the teams making one of those offers. Having Bauers back for one season would be great, because if he is unable to replicate his career year, they would be clear of him. There is a chance that his 2026 season ends up being something like Trent Grisham's 2025 season. Every team will need to decide whether they believe Bauers has finally figured out the big leagues with his new approach to the game or if last season was a fluke. The rest of the league may let the Brewers be the team that has to figure it out by making Bauers accept the qualifying offer. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! As far as keeping Bauers past next season, the Brewers have no need to. Not only do they have Andrew Fischer, Blake Burke and Luke Adams capable of playing first base knocking on the door of the big leagues, but they also have Andrew Vaughn who could be a potential option past next season. Bauers will be expensive to keep on a multi-year deal, and could really block some prospects the team views fondly. The Brewers should not change the way they do business just because they won the World Series. Bauers was a great player for them, and his efforts won't be forgotten. Ultimately, bringing him back for one more year won't hurt their long-term plans, and it will minimize the damage if his breakout proves to be a fluke. More MLB: Braves-Rangers Blockbuster Trade Idea Would Net Braves Two Superstars, Help Rangers Achieve Goal

item.description: The 2027 recruiting cycle still has a few weeks to go until National Signing Day, but a majority of the top classes in the nation are set. item.title: As Greg Schiano’s future hangs in balance, Rutgers fans have minds made up: ‘We need a change’
item.description: SHI Stadium was half-empty as Rutgers hosted a Big Ten blueblood, but those who made the trek to Piscataway made their voices heard. There were loud, sustained boos following a controversial call from the officials. There was a jubilant celebration as the final minutes of a close game ticked off the clock. There were frequent chants to fire an underperforming coach. The problem for the Scarlet Knights : all of that noise came from the visiting Michigan fans. Along with a 28-21 win on the field , the Wolverines (5-3, 2-3) blew out Rutgers (2-6, 1-4) in the stands on Saturday. Rutgers +17.5 point spread is currently sitting at -116 on ProphetX for Saturday’s Big Ten clash versus Michigan. Also, view our helpful guide to the best sportsbook promos to shop for competitive odds. Michigan fans made up at least half of a crowd that was announced at 39,540, the lowest official attendance at SHI Stadium for a non-COVID Big Ten game since head coach Greg Schiano returned in the 2020 season. Despite their team stumbling through a mediocre season, Michigan fans brought plenty of life into a moribund building. Rutgers fans, meanwhile, spoke with their absence. “I really don’t worry about things I can’t control,” Schiano said following the game. “I have enough of my own issues that I have to work on. I just try to do that. As I’ve always told you guys, I’m grateful for the ones that came, because those people, they’re supporting us through thick and thin. We’ve had thick here and we’re a little bit thin right now.” Two years removed from reaching a second straight bowl game and appearing to be on an upward trajectory, the Scarlet Knights are barreling toward their worst record of Schiano’s second stint after going 5-7 last fall. After getting upset by UMass , beaten by Boston College , fall short against USC and get blown out by Northwestern and Indiana — with wins over FCS Howard and last-place Maryland in between — Rutgers will need to win two of their final four games to match the 4-8 mark of the 2022 season. They are projected to be underdogs in their next three games (at Wisconsin, vs. Nebraska, at Penn State). Rutgers has one of the worst defenses in the country again , and despite having two of the best skill players in college football in wide receiver KJ Duff and running back Antwan Raymond, its offense is mediocre, ranking 73rd nationally in points per game. The Scarlet Knights, who are 7-13 overall since the start of the 2025 season, have lost their last four Big Ten home games and they are 3-9 in their last 12 conference games in Piscataway. They have lost 24 of their last 28 games as underdogs of more than a field goal , have not defeated a ranked opponent in 17 years and have not been ranked in 14 years. Barring a shocking 4-0 finish to the regular season, Rutgers will miss a bowl game — the minimum tangible mark for the improvement that athletic director Keli Zinn said she wanted to see from last fall — for a second straight year. The piling losses — particularly the shocking 16-point defeat to the Minutemen — and poor play have put Schiano’s job into question. He is on one of the hottest seats in college football , and now, even the most loyal fans are calling for Rutgers to move on from the winningest coach in program history. “I love the guy. I have pictures of him handing us pizza (before the 2006 Louisville game). But we need a change,” Vijay Ahlawat, a Class of 2010 alum and 12-year season ticket holder, told NJ.com from his tailgate in the yellow lot. “It’s time. It’s played its course. ... He came, stabilized the program, got them to a decent level. The last couple of years, we’ve gotten stagnant, and now it’s all fallen apart.” Rutgers fans surveyed by NJ.com prior to the game against Michigan — both in person and on social media — largely share in Ahlawat’s sentiments, and a close loss to Michigan was not enough to change their opinions. But there is no guarantee that the growing list of fans who want to see change get their wish this offseason. The Scarlet Knights would have to pay roughly $28 million over the next three years to Schiano ($18 million) and his coaching staff ($10 million) if they make a move — a sizable total for an athletic department that is running a $516 million deficit over the past 11 years and that hopes to expand its football stadium in the near future. The University is also in the middle of contract negotiations with various employee unions. While not an insurmountable number, it is a major reason for growing momentum behind Schiano’s return during the 2027 season, with multiple people with knowledge of the situation putting the odds of a change at 50/50 with a month remaining in the campaign. Asked by NJ.com where he believes he stands in his job security, Schiano said Tuesday that he doesn’t “give that any thought.” “I really don’t,” he said. “I’m focused on Wisconsin, I’m focused on recruiting. I’m focused on the portal, the things that my job entails. And we’re going to be great. I’m excited about the future.” When Rutgers retained head coach Chris Ash for a fourth season in 2019 despite a 2-10 record the previous season, it sold 16,585 season tickets — a 27% drop from the previous season and 7,678 less than it sold this fall. Anecdotally, a majority of fans surveyed by NJ.com said that they planned to keep their season tickets through gritted teeth if the Scarlet Knights keep the status quo. “It’s a placeholder on the calendar,” Steve Cross, a class of 1988 alum who has had season tickets since 1989, told NJ.com. “If Greg was still here, (my tailgate group) would still show up.” But nothing revealed the fanbase’s current feeling better than the stands at SHI Stadium on Saturday, which had as much maize-and-blue as scarlet. The most telling moment came in the fourth quarter, when a controversial kick-catch interference penalty on a fair catch prevented a Rutgers turnover. The visiting fans booed for multiple plays, getting so loud on third down that Rutgers had to call a timeout to regroup. Just as boisterous were the chants to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck when his unit stumbled early in the game, as well as the “Let’s Go Blue!” chants in the final two minutes after the Wolverines clinched the win. MORE BY BRIAN FONSECA Rutgers basketball launches cancer research fundraising initiative led by Steve Pikiell Nov. 3, 2026, 10:11 a.m. How Dylan Grant, other Rutgers basketball transfers performed in 1st game with new team in 2026-27 season Nov. 3, 2026, 9:09 a.m. The same scene could play out in Rutgers’ next home game against Nebraska, another blueblood program with a massive fanbase that travels well. The saving grace for the Scarlet Knights is that the Cornhuskers wear red, too. And unless Rutgers springs an upset, the desire for a clean slate from the home fans will only get stronger. “The problem is that the guy has had basically 17 years. If it wasn’t for Rutgers the second time around, he probably would not have a head coaching job,” Cross said. “People have to realize — and I think the school has realized — he’s basically had two decades. He’s not the guy.” Read the original article on NJ.com . Add NJ.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: Dianna Russini finally returning to sports media after Mike Vrabel scandal
item.description: Next week will mark the halfway point in the NFL season, and apparently, also the return of Dianna Russini to sports media after she stepped down from her role with The Athletic in the wake of the scandal involving her and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel that dominated the offseason. “Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic ’s standards,” The Athletic’s Mike Semel, who conducted an internal investigation, said of the controversy. “Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed.” According to Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio, a “source with knowledge of the situation” has made it known that Russini has made it clear to people around the league that she’ll make her return “next week” The news comes after Russini reportedly hired infamous publicist Melissa Nathan, a veteran of multiple infamous Hollywood imbroglios, but one who isn’t without her own controversy, as she is facing perjury allegations due to her involvement in the incredibly messy situation between Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni. Many prominent figures across sports media also anticipated that Russini’s return to sports media was imminent. In August, Mike Silver sang her praises and predicted her return. “Really good friend of mine,” he said of Russini. “Worked with her at The Athletic for too short of a time, unfortunately. Really, really proud of the journalism we did together and honestly just really bummed that we don’t get to continue it because we worked really well together. “I don’t think people understand the level of elite that she was performing at in terms of keeping in touch with the really important people around the league. And I don’t mean just agents and transactional, like players, coaches, owners, all of it, talking, having real conversations with them every day and really knowing what was going on and competing at a very high level. “I do miss having her a lot. Very bummed that it all imploded. She became a very high-profile person. I’m not a super judgy person. I would never comment on tabloid crap.” Silver then praised her family, and predicted that when she returned, it’d be in a role other than an NFL insider. “And I do think she’s going to be back, probably not as an insider, at least in the short term. But I think she’ll be back in this realm, probably talking about football and other things pretty soon,” he said. It would seem we’ll know immenently just what capacity she’ll be back in. The post Dianna Russini finally returning to sports media after Mike Vrabel scandal appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

Really, really proud of the journalism we did together and honestly just really bummed that we don’t get to continue it because we worked really well together. “I don’t think people understand the level of elite that she was performing at in terms of keeping in touch with the really important people around the league. And I don’t mean just agents and transactional, like players, coaches, owners, all of it, talking, having real conversations with them every day and really knowing what was going on and competing at a very high level. “I do miss having her a lot. Very bummed that it all imploded. She became a very high-profile person. I’m not a super judgy person. I would never comment on tabloid crap.” Silver then praised her family, and predicted that when she returned, it’d be in a role other than an NFL insider. “And I do think she’s going to be back, probably not as an insider, at least in the short term. But I think she’ll be back in this realm, probably talking about football and other things pretty soon,” he said. It would seem we’ll know immenently just what capacity she’ll be back in. The post Dianna Russini finally returning to sports media after Mike Vrabel scandal appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Could Queen City Quarter become an everyday destination in Uptown Charlotte?
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets are part of an ownership group that purchased the former EpiCentre complex in Uptown Charlotte, now known as Queen City Quarter, for $27.5 million. The purchase price covers a property with an estimated value of nearly $100 million. Sports analysts consider the three-company venture well financed. Erik Spanberg, a reporter with the Sports Business Journal, noted that the acquisition follows earlier municipal approvals for facility upgrades. “I don’t think many of us knew that the Charlotte Hornets were going to be part of the buying group,” Spanberg said. He added that “it started when the city approved the arena renovations and the training center,” explaining that “teams want to surround their arenas and stadiums with things that they develop and own.” PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Former EpiCentre site Queen City Quarter undergoes major change Rick Schnall, co-owner of the Charlotte Hornets, hinted in May that broader developments were being considered alongside basketball facilities. “From the beginning, this project is more than it is not just about basketball,” Schnall said. “It’s about continuing momentum in Uptown Charlotte in the city of Charlotte and strengthening the Spectrum Center and the community around it.” Other NBA franchises have pursued similar arena-adjacent real estate projects. In 2015, the Sacramento Kings entered a joint venture to redevelop a plaza into 1 million square feet of space known as Downtown Commons, or DOCO, surrounding the Golden one Center. According to the developer, that project influenced $6.7 billion in new projects by 2022, while bringing 150 retail businesses, residential units, hotels, restaurants, and increased foot traffic to the area. Spanberg noted that multiple franchises have executed comparable development projects around their venues. “In the NBA, you’ve seen not only Sacramento, but you’ve also seen Milwaukee Bucks do it really well with the beer district. You’ve seen the Indiana Pacers do it recently,” Spanberg said. He added that the long-term challenge for such projects lies in sustained activity. “The question always is, can you do it to an extent where people want to come not just on game day, but every day,” Spanberg said. Similar developments are also underway elsewhere in North Carolina. A new entertainment district is planned in Raleigh surrounding the Lenovo Center. According to the Sports Business Journal , those plans feature thousands of housing units, dining areas, and an enhanced tailgating experience for Carolina Hurricanes fans.

item.title: Big Ten classes in the Rivals Industry Team Recruiting Rankings
item.description: The 2027 recruiting cycle still has a few weeks to go until National Signing Day, but a majority of the top classes in the nation are set. While coaching changes, changes of heart and other factors may lead to some flips down the stretch, for the most part, top recruits look locked into their respective pledges. Oregon leads the Big Ten with the fourth-ranked class nationally in the Rivals Industry Team Recruiting Rankings , and the conference as a whole has nine of the top 25 classes. item.title: Sabres Get Reality Check on Dylan Larkin Trade
item.description: Larkin Red Wings Getty The Buffalo Sabres are a good team that is trying to return to the playoffs after breaking a 15-year drought. That’s going to have their fanbase circling every big name that might be available in an effort to improve the roster, and that includes Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin. Larkin requested a trade after last season ended, but he still hasn’t been moved. At first, Larkin was playing for the Red Wings to start this season, but that has stopped — he’s now not expected to play until he gets traded. The calendar is into November, though, and Larkin hasn’t been moved yet. The Sabres aren’t on Larkin’s 10-team approved trade list, yet that hasn’t stopped speculation that he could still end up in Buffalo. That idea came crashing down on Wednesday when The Athletic’s Matthew Fairburn weighed in. Sabres’ Dylan Larkin Trade Update Fairburn didn’t hold back in breaking down the potential for a Larkin deal. First, he explained that he understands how the thinking can get here. “Trades are fun, especially in a league where free agency has become even more watered down over the years,” Fairburn writes. “So I get why people want to throw ideas around and play general manager. And I do think it’s fair to expect Kekäläinen to make a significant deal at some point this season. He’s circled around a few doozies this calendar year between Colton Parayko and Connor Hellebuyck.” Despite that, Fairburn isn’t convinced the Sabres and Larkin will come together. “That said, the idea of Larkin might be a non-starter,” Fairburn writes. “The Sabres have the assets to pull it off and have had conversations with the Red Wings about those assets. But Kekäläinen is the type to have those conversations about any big-name player who’s available. He wouldn’t be doing his job otherwise. Larkin would fill arguably their most glaring need for a No. 1 center and comes at a reasonable cap hit. But the Sabres are not on his expanded 10-team trade list . How much will that list have to expand before Buffalo ends up on it? Are the Sabres even a more attractive option than simply staying in Detroit? Yes, Buffalo ended its playoff drought, but that’s still just one year. Assuming he doesn’t want to go to a Canadian team, that leaves 26 teams. I wonder if the Sabres would get on the list if it got to 15 teams? Would it take 20? And how much more would the Sabres have to pay for the Red Wings to be compelled to move him within the division? All of those questions make me hesitant to get people too excited about the idea. I also think the Sabres should be wary about adding a player who essentially needs to be begged to come to Buffalo. You don’t want to be someone’s 15th choice when you’re giving up the assets required to get a player like Larkin.” Why Dylan Larkin Hasn’t Been Traded The analysis by Fairburn explains part of what’s happening here, and specifically why the Sabres might not make sense. But in general, it appears Detroit can’t find a fitting trade

Detroit doesn’t seem to want to enter a total rebuild, though, so the Red Wings would want current NHL talent in return. It doesn’t seem like it’ll get resolved anytime soon, but even when it does, don’t count on the Sabres being involved. item.title: 'The objective is clear' - Aston Villa send firm message to Manchester United as Unai Emery commits beyond 2029
item.description: Unai Emery Aston Villa - Getty Aston Villa have publicly confirmed that Unai Emery is committed to the club beyond 2029 after positive talks with chairman Nassef Sawiris, ending speculation over a move to Manchester United. The Spaniard has been strongly linked with replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, where Villa travel this weekend in need of a response to Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League defeat to Barcelona. Aston Villa confirm Emery commitment amid Manchester United links Villa have moved to end speculation over Emery's future, releasing a statement on Wednesday that confirmed a clear commitment beyond 2029 following talks between the manager and club chiefs. The 55-year-old has been strongly linked with replacing Carrick at Manchester United . According to The Telegraph, Emery is in advanced talks over a new deal at Villa, which would nip rumours of a move to Old Trafford in the bud. It would have cost United £20 million to release him from his current contract. Villa statement reveals details of key meeting Emery's impressive four-year spell at Villa prompted talks with Sawiris, president of football operations Roberto Olabe and director of football operations Damian Vidagany over his long-term future. In a very transparent statement, the club confirmed the meeting had produced "positive discussions", with their update reading: "Aston Villa held an important working meeting today to plan the club's future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project. "The meeting brought together Nassef Sawiris, the club's Chairman and Unai Emery alongside President of Football Operations Roberto Olabe and Director of Football Operations Damian Vidagany. Emery set to stay at Villa into the next decade "The discussions focused on jointly planning the club's long-term strategic direction, with positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery based on the shared ambitions and common goal to reach excellency and keep growing during the next years. "The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements." Emery signed a five-year contract extension in May 2024, 18 months after joining, but he now looks set to remain in charge heading into the next decade. What next for Emery, Villa and Carrick? Emery will be at Old Trafford this weekend when United host Villa, whose 3-0 loss to Barcelona and draw with Fulham last Saturday leave them needing a positive result before the November international break. United had won just two games all season before Tuesday's sensational 3-2 comeback triumph over AS Roma, and another victory could keep Carrick in the role beyond the break, when his performances are due to be reviewed.

item.title: Hornets Reveal Kon Knueppel’s Final Status Ahead of Nets Matchup
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 28: Kon Knueppel #7 poses for a photo opportunity during the Charlotte Hornets Media Day at Novant Health Performance Center on September 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Charlotte Hornets (3-5) are struggling to gain footing at the beginning of the 2026-27 season. Charlotte currently holds the worst offense in the NBA eight games in. There’s reasoning behind this current mark, including in early injuries to core players. Two of the five starting players for the Hornets (Coby White, Kon Knueppel) have been out thus far due to different injuries. In a sign of progress, Charlotte is making a final call on the latter as of Wednesday afternoon. Hornets Make Final Call on Star Wing The Hornets official PR account ( via X ) is ruling that Knueppel will make his season debut on Wednesday against the Brooklyn Nets . Knueppel, 21, has been working his way back from a left hamstring strain. The season debut is setting up to be a major breath of fresh air for a Charlotte offense that needs life. Knueppel’s season debut should carry much weight. His 273 three-point connections as a rookie led the NBA. This, along with progression that should come with more experience alongside teammates such as Brandon Miller , should breed more positive results. What Knueppel’s Return Means For Rest of Rotation The obvious fallout from Knueppel coming back is that he will obviously be in the starting lineup. However, there are deeper implications than just starting. Players that were seeing a decent volume of playing time have a chance to sink in the rotation. The player that might face the most negative impact is Grayson Allen . Allen, a Duke alum the same as Knueppel, has been the early-season alternative – particularly as a three-point marksmen. The immediate need for Allen to eat minutes subsides now, although he still provides value as a playmaker. It will be fascinating to see how head coach Charles Lee operates in this situation. item.content:encoded: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 28: Kon Knueppel #7 poses for a photo opportunity during the Charlotte Hornets Media Day at Novant Health Performance Center on September 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Charlotte Hornets (3-5) are struggling to gain footing at the beginning of the 2026-27 season. Charlotte currently holds the worst offense in the NBA eight games in. There’s reasoning behind this current mark, including in early injuries to core players. Two of the five starting players for the Hornets (Coby White, Kon Knueppel) have been out thus far due to different injuries. In a sign of progress, Charlotte is making a final call on the latter as of Wednesday afternoon. Hornets Make Final Call on Star Wing The Hornets official PR account ( via X ) is ruling that Knueppel will make his season debut on Wednesday against the Brooklyn Nets . Knueppel, 21, has been working his way back from a left hamstring strain. The season debut is setting up to be a major breath of fresh air for a Charlotte offense that needs life. Knueppel’s season debut should carry much weight. His 273 three-point connections as a rookie led the NBA. This, along with progression that should come with more experience alongside teammates such as Brandon Miller , should breed more positive results. What Knueppel’s Return Means For Rest of Rotation The obvious fallout from Knueppel coming back is that he will obviously be in the starting lineup. However, there are deeper implications than just starting. Players that were seeing a decent volume of playing time have a chance to sink in the rotation. The player that might face the most negative impact is Grayson Allen . Allen, a Duke alum the same as Knueppel, has been the early-season alternative – particularly as a three-point marksmen. The immediate need for Allen to eat minutes subsides now, although he still provides value as a playmaker. It will be fascinating to see how head coach Charles Lee operates in this situation. Hornets-Nets is slating for a 7:30 P.M. EST tip-off. item.title: Nigerian footballer Quadri Liameed discharged from hospital after head kick in Spain
item.description: Nigerian midfielder Quadri Liameed has been discharged from hospital after medical tests ruled out serious injuries following a head kick during Sabadell’s match against Albacete in Spain. The 24-year-old initially lost consciousness after being struck in the head by Albacete player José Corpas during the 43rd minute of the encounter at the Carlos Belmonte Stadium. Liameed later regained consciousness and was taken to hospital for medical examinations, raising concerns among his teammates, club officials and football supporters. However, Sabadell confirmed that the midfielder had received medical clearance shortly after midnight after further tests returned reassuring results. In a statement published on its official X account, the club said, “The best of the news has arrived! “@Qlimeed has received medical discharge after all the tests have come out well and will return tonight to Sabadell! “We want to thank the medical services of @AlbaceteBPSAD for the help received at all times.” The midfielder returned to Sabadell by car, accompanied by a member of the club’s medical staff, and went home to rest. According to reports, the concussion protocol was deactivated after the medical examinations ruled out any injury, meaning he did not need to remain under observation overnight. Liameed is expected to follow a specialised training programme over the next few days before fully rejoining his teammates. The incident occurred after Corpas struck Liameed in the head with his boot while attempting to reach the ball, prompting an immediate medical response and his subsequent removal from the pitch. The post Nigerian footballer Quadri Liameed discharged from hospital after head kick in Spain appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Everything Luke Fickell said after Badgers loss to Iowa
item.description: Wisconsin head coach Luke Fickell leads his team to the field before their game against Notre Dame Sunday, September 6, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Wisconsin Badgers were embarrassed 30-0 by the Iowa Hawkeyes in yet another rivalry game flop, as they fell to 5-3 on the season and 3-2 in conference play. It was a game where Wisconsin lost on every side and was awfully reminiscent of the team’s previous two losses to Iowa. Luke Fickell has now been outscored 124-16 in his four games at Wisconsin against Iowa. After the game, Fickell spoke with the media, outlining his frustrations and sharing his thoughts on the game. Here’s everything he said after the loss on Saturday. Opening Statement Well, that’s an old-fashioned ass whooping, and it doesn’t feel good. Were we prepared? Were we not prepared? We didn’t play like we were prepared today. They asked me if there were any positives, and I said I don’t know that I could find any positives in the way that we played, the way we performed. Yeah, they kept battling no matter what, but that’s a foregone conclusion. You have to do that. It’s, do you battle with the intent? Do you have the intensity to understand what it’s going to be like when you walk into this place and what you have to do in order to not just win, but make this a game? And we did none of that today. It’s very, very disappointing. I’m not sitting here saying I’ve got any answers for you. I’m not pointing any fingers at anybody because all three phases of the game, we were completely manhandled for 60-plus minutes. On why this keeps happening vs. Iowa… I don’t know. We made an overemphasis on it in the past, on the rivalry and what we needed to be able to do all of spring football and all of winter and all of fall. And then this year, it’s like, look, let’s make sure we understand, we respect the rivalry, but we don’t overdo something that is going to put us in a position where we play too emotional and can’t play 60-plus minutes. And we didn’t do that either. I think first of all, you’ve got to win the line of scrimmage. And I know that we can honestly say for the last couple years, we have not done that. And so anything beyond that, there’s a lot of other things, but that’s where it starts and that’s where it has been. On whether Iowa’s recent dominance has affected Wisconsin’s confidence in the rivalry… No, I don’t. There’s so many guys here that don’t even know or understand what’s happened the last couple years. We explained it and talked about it and went through some of those things, but they didn’t live it. So it’s not like they have some shell shock of some remembrance of what has happened. I don’t think that’s the case. It’s just the sheer fact that we didn’t play today. Whether there’s an arrogance and a delusion coming off of last week that we felt like we were in a different place, I hope we have more maturity than that. But surely it didn’t look like it today. Do you have the intensity to understand what it’s going to be like when you walk into this place and what you have to do in order to not just win, but make this a game? And we did none of that today. It’s very, very disappointing. I’m not sitting here saying I’ve got any answers for you. I’m not pointing any fingers at anybody because all three phases of the game, we were completely manhandled for 60-plus minutes. On why this keeps happening vs. Iowa… I don’t know. We made an overemphasis on it in the past, on the rivalry and what we needed to be able to do all of spring football and all of winter and all of fall. And then this year, it’s like, look, let’s make sure we understand, we respect the rivalry, but we don’t overdo something that is going to put us in a position where we play too emotional and can’t play 60-plus minutes. And we didn’t do that either. I think first of all, you’ve got to win the line of scrimmage. And I know that we can honestly say for the last couple years, we have not done that. And so anything beyond that, there’s a lot of other things, but that’s where it starts and that’s where it has been. On whether Iowa’s recent dominance has affected Wisconsin’s confidence in the rivalry… No, I don’t. There’s so many guys here that don’t even know or understand what’s happened the last couple years. We explained it and talked about it and went through some of those things, but they didn’t live it. So it’s not like they have some shell shock of some remembrance of what has happened. I don’t think that’s the case. It’s just the sheer fact that we didn’t play today. Whether there’s an arrogance and a delusion coming off of last week that we felt like we were in a different place, I hope we have more maturity than that. But surely it didn’t look like it today. On the decision to replace Colton Joseph at quarterback… I just thought it was an opportunity, and it was some time we needed to try to find a way to have a little bit of a spark. The situation was where it was. We weren’t able to run the football, so we felt like, hey, look, I don’t know that we need to keep Colton in there and keep trying to run him to see if he can get us going. Let’s give the young kid an opportunity. Let’s see if we can find any spark and some things that we need to see. On whether the quarterback change provided a spark and what the team needs to improve… I don’t know. I think we do need to see the way people are playing us. Either way, we’ve talked about this. If we don’t continue to understand that we have to get better each and every week, then no, we will not be who we want to be.And whether you take a really disappointing loss or you have an incredible emotional victory, either way, you’ve got to be able to ingest it. You’ve got to be able to apply it. You’ve got to be able to grow from it. And this one’s going to be a hell of a lot harder to grow from because there’s going to be some glaring things on film that we haven’t seen all year. But they’re real because if you put them on film, you’ve got to own them. And I think that’s where we’re going to have to challenge ourselves maturity-wise to see if we can take a good hard look at ourselves and recognize some of the things that I thought we were doing better and we were getting better at, but we did not do today. On the decision to go for it on fourth-and-goal… Let’s score a touchdown. I don’t know there’s anything more. Had they called a false start there, which we probably did false start, and it would have been fourth-and-five, we probably would have had to kick it. It wasn’t going to be the situation where, outside of probably three right there, that we were going to be willing to go for it. We had to have some momentum, generate some energy, but we got the thing inside the 1-yard line, and there was no doubt we were going. On Iowa scoring on a similar play to Wisconsin’s failed fourth-and-goal attempt… We didn’t set an edge. They did a decent job setting an edge, and then they triggered and made the play inside. We were a little bit out of whack, out of sorts. I don’t know that we were all in sync as the ball was snapped, which is on us. But that probably had something to do with us not executing really well. On the false starts and other mistakes offensively… No, I don’t even know if that’s the most maddening. The big plays defensively are as maddening as anything. Those guys did an unbelievable job of working on the cadence and the noise all week. We did it all week for the Penn State game. We did it all week this week. I don’t even know that it was that, because I don’t know that it was like it was two years ago in the night game. So if there’s four or five of them, we’re not in a position where we’re going to be able to overcome a lot of those things. But I think that’s a little bit more just on us. It wasn’t something that I think those guys didn’t do a great job preparing for. They just did a really bad job at executing that. On whether Wisconsin’s slow start snowballed throughout the game… Yeah, I don’t know. Gosh, you get them into third-and-seven or third-and-eight on the very first series, and you’re in a position where this is where you’ve been good. And you give up a big play, and that just is a little bit more uncharacteristic of us. We’ve been pretty good, and even in those situations, if guys get first downs, they haven’t given up big plays, and they’ve found ways to make the big plays. And then from there, I think it did continue to snowball a little bit in the sense that maybe we started to get antsy, maybe we started to push, maybe we started to press a little bit because we weren’t able to get to him. We weren’t able to make him uncomfortable in the pocket. And so what they did most of the day was give him an opportunity to do what he needed to do from a pretty comfortable pocket. On what he would say to fans concerned about the direction of the program… Well, I think that we’re a work in progress, and it’s all about getting better. One game doesn’t define you. One moment doesn’t define you. And so I think for us, it’s always been about climbing a mountain. It’s always been about, hey, how are we going to get better? How are we going to continue to push this thing to be where we want to be when it comes to crunch time? I felt like we’ve been moving that needle in the right direction. I feel like that’s what we’ve got within that locker room, and today was not that. And so it’s very disappointing, and it’s very difficult. But that’s also part of the game. I think if there’s one thing, unfortunately, you do try to learn from others around college football, that you’ve got to come out every single week because anybody can do anything on any given weekend.
